source: Itasca Software 9.6 documentation, 'Comparison of FLAC2D to SHAKE for a Layered, Linear-Elastic Soil Deposit' (https://docs.itascasoftware.com/itasca960/flac3d/zone/test2d/Dynamic/F2ShakeLinearElasticCase/F2ShakeLinearElasticCase.html) — case derived from the SHAKE-91 distribution (Idriss & Sun 1992; NISEE https://nisee.berkeley.edu/elibrary/software.html)

published.note: surface peak acceleration; published agreement between the two external codes

halfspace.note: 3x-Vs elastic stand-in for the driven base (Itasca drives a fixed base; elastic-bedrock outcrop reproduces the published peak within tolerance)

input.calibrationNote: peak of the analytic form at t=3.75 s corresponds to 0.2 g per the Itasca page

nonlinearTenLayer.note: the FLAC3D nonlinear-elastic page documents the SHAKE-91 10-layer example deposit (150 ft, clay/sand G-Gmax curves, Loma Prieta DIAM.ACC input) — reserved for the R7 continuous-regression protocol (requires the NISEE input record)

ourResult.method: analytic input x Physics.shTransferFunction (Thomson-Haskell, 10% hysteretic damping), inverse DFT peak; measured 2026-08-25
